candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: exceptDate
candidates.comment: An exception date relation between a schedule and a specific date or datetime when a scheduled event will not take place. Also called: exclusion date, cancelled date, unavailable date. Examples: "Weekly Yoga Class Schedule" except date "2023-12-25", "Daily Bus Route Schedule" except date "2024-01-01T08:00:00", "Monthly Book Club Schedule" except date "2023-11-11".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: dateIssued
candidates.comment: A temporal issuance relation between a ticket and the date it was issued. Also called: issuance date, date of issue, ticket date. Examples: "Concert Ticket" date issued "2023-04-01", "Flight Ticket" date issued "2023-01-10T14:30:00Z", "Parking Permit" date issued "2023-07-01".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: dateSent
candidates.comment: A temporal dispatch relation between a message and the date/time it was sent. Also called: sending date, message dispatch time, transmission time. Examples: "Email" date sent "2023-10-26T10:20:00Z", "SMS Message" date sent "2023-10-26T10:30:00Z". Distinct from dateReceived, which is when the message arrived.

candidates.label: eventStatus

candidates.label: location

Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: foodEvent
candidates.comment: A food event relation between a cook action and the specific food-related event where the cooking took place. Also called: culinary event, cooking event, gastronomic occasion. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food event "Annual Food Festival", "Home Cook makes dinner" food event "Family Dinner Party", "Baker bakes bread" food event "Charity Bake Sale". Distinct from foodEstablishment, which is a specific place.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

chosen_property.label: isA
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that an entity is a type of another entity (broader category).
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses a general 'is a' relationship between two entities of the same type for sub-categorization. Minting a new property.

candidates.label: isrcCode
candidates.comment: A music recording identification relation between a music recording and its International Standard Recording Code. Also called ISRC identifier, recording code, music track ID. Examples: A music recording has an isrcCode of 'US-S1Z-99-00001'. A song has an isrcCode of 'GB-LFB-04-00001'. An album track has an isrcCode of 'QZ-F89-12-00001'. Distinct from iswcCode, which is for musical compositions, not recordings.

candidates.label: isBasedOnUrl
candidates.comment: A source URL relation between a creative work and a specific URL that served as a resource for its creation. Also called source URL, derived from URL, based on URL, reference URL. Examples: A research paper has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1234.5678'. A blog post has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://example.com/original-article'. A web page has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://old-version.com/page'. Distinct from isBasedOn, which can refer to any CreativeWork or Product, not just a URL.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: isResizable
candidates.comment: A model property relation indicating whether a 3D model can be scaled or resized. Also called resizable, scalable, adjustable size. Examples: A 3D model of a chair has isResizable set to 'true'. A 3D model of a building has isResizable set to 'false'. A 3D model of a character has isResizable set to 'true'.

candidates.label: iswcCode
candidates.comment: A music composition identification relation between a music composition and its International Standard Musical Work Code. Also called ISWC identifier, composition code, musical work ID. Examples: A music composition has an iswcCode of 'T-034.045.001-6'. A song has an iswcCode of 'T-901.234.567-8'. A classical piece has an iswcCode of 'T-123.456.789-0'. Distinct from isrcCode, which is for music recordings, not compositions.

candidates.label: isicV4
candidates.comment: An industry classification relation between an organization, person, or place and its International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 4 code. Also called ISIC code, industry classification code, economic activity code. Examples: An organization has an isicV4 of '6201' (Computer programming activities). A person has an isicV4 of '8620' (Medical and dental practice activities). A place has an isicV4 of '5510' (Hotels and similar accommodation).

candidates.label: isProprietary
candidates.comment: A naming status relation indicating whether a dietary supplement or drug is identified by a proprietary or brand name. Also called brand name, proprietary name, trademarked name. Examples: A drug has isProprietary set to 'true' (e.g., Tylenol). A dietary supplement has isProprietary set to 'false' (e.g., Acetaminophen). A medication has isProprietary set to 'true'. Distinct from isAvailableGenerically, which indicates if a generic *form* exists, not if the *name* itself is proprietary.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: isVariantOf
candidates.comment: A product variation relation between a product or product model and the base product or product group from which it is a specific variant. Also called variant of, version of, derived from product, specific model of. Examples: A 'red iPhone 15' isVariantOf 'iPhone 15 Pro'. A 'size L t-shirt' isVariantOf 'Basic T-Shirt ProductGroup'. A 'diesel car model' isVariantOf 'Car Model X'. Distinct from isRelatedTo or isSimilarTo, as it implies a direct hierarchical relationship of variation from a base product or group.

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: identifyingExam

candidates.label: assesses

candidates.label: itemReviewed

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: question
candidates.comment: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."
